title: Gate Shift
user: Players seeking a tactile, original, browser-friendly logic puzzle with a satisfying finite run rather than a familiar word, merge, or match-three loop.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A detailed beta request presents a new grid slider in which rotating rows and columns through fixed gates creates, changes, or removes tiles, with scoring based on empty space and moves left.
A 2026 itch.io browser-game release frames a small original interaction—bouncing bullets and territory control—as immediately playable in the browser rather than an install.

recurrence: The first thread is a concrete request for feedback on a nonstandard grid mechanic; the second shows indie creators are still bringing compact, mechanic-led games to the browser in 2026.
current_workaround: Play polished but repetitive word/merge games, download an experimental mobile beta, or use puzzle apps that blend finite boards into endless retention loops.
incumbents_and_gap: Threes/2048, sliding blocks, and match games own familiar operations, but they rarely give a short authored campaign with reversible state and an explicit finish. Existing puzzle apps also commonly put experimental games behind an install.
smallest_useful_product: A browser puzzle about rotating six conveyor rings through fixed color gates. A level takes 4–10 minutes and ends after a fixed move budget; every rotation can be previewed, but choosing a shortcut changes future gate polarity. Each run draws one of three deterministic board layouts and a daily challenge. Inputs: swipe, arrows, undo. Non-goals: procedurally infinite boards, match-three monetization, copied mechanics/art, and social ranking in v1.
success_measure: At least 50% of players finish the tutorial board, 25% complete three boards, and the median session reaches a deliberate level ending rather than a quit.
monetization: one-time — a finite set of authored puzzles is a cleaner fit than ads or move sales.
constraints: Puzzle generator must prove target levels solvable; offer undo without penalty; respect reduced-motion settings and make color nonessential through symbols.
why_distinct: The interesting unit is reversible gate-state planning with a hard ending, not another tile-merging or generic slider clone.
